To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed gate driver with the RSCS is able to detect short-circuits and reconstruct phase currents for SiC MOSFETS in 1.2kV, 300A half-bridge module.

a gate-driver-integrated RSCS is able to detect short-circuit fault and reconstruct phase current of a 1,200 V, 300 A half-bridge module, with an error of less than 1% and 3% respectively, and a bandwidth of 100 kHz, which can be further improved by increasing the number of RSCS.
the RSCS-based gate driver can detect short circuit with high accuracy and low false alarm rate, as well as reconstruct phase current with high accuracy and good dynamic response.

the integration of a Rogowski coil sensor with the gate driver to enable the gate-driver-level intelligence for SiC-based power modules.
the development of a gate driver with integrated current sensors and the demonstration of its benefits in a SiC-based power inverter.
the gate-driver-level intelligence that can improve the reliability of SiC power inverters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RSCS is capable of detecting a short-circuit fault and estimating the phase-current waveform in the inverter, and that this capability can be integrated on the gate-driver PCB of any half-bridge module.
the RSCS integrated on the gate-driver is a promising technology for future SiC-based inverter systems.
the RSCS is an enabling sensor for SiC MOSFETS and can be used for various applications in the gate-driver level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RSCS-based gate driver is capable of providing accurate phase-current sensing for the control of SiC-based power inverter.
a low-cost and high-performance gate-driver-integrated current sensor is demonstrated for the SiC MOSFETS.
the proposed gate-driver-level intelligence is promising for SiC MOSFETS and can be extended to other wide-bandgap devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the RSCS can be a promising alternative to Hall sensors and current probes for phase current sensing in SiC-based motor drives, which can be easily embedded on gate driver boards and thus can be used for short-circuited detection and fault protection.
gate-driver-integrated RSCS are a promising solution for the future of high-voltage SiC-based power electronics.
the RSCS can be a promising solution for the gate-driver level of SiC-based power electronics, where the intelligence of power electronics can be brought closer to the power semiconductor.
